key_insight: MAGNet is a Transformer-style graph neural network that adaptively learns multi-scale interactions between brain structure and function, producing unified, interpretable representations that improve cognitive prediction and insight.
problem_solved: Jointly modeling complementary structural and functional connectomes is hard because they operate at different scales and modalities; MAGNet addresses adaptive cross-modal alignment and multi-scale interaction learning to capture how morphology and connectivity together relate to cognition.
method: Transformer-style graph neural network with adaptive multi-scale graph attention that learns cross-node and cross-scale interactions.
Extracts inter-regional morphological features via source-based morphometry (structural MRI) and fuses them with functional connectivity graphs using attention-guided message passing.
Multi-scale aggregation and interpretable attention maps allow identification of region-level structure–function contributions to cognitive traits.
impact: Provides a generalizable multimodal graph representation framework that boosts predictive performance and interpretability in neuroimaging tasks, and can be applied by ML practitioners to other structured multimodal problems where adaptive cross-modal relationships matter.
visual_elements: Architecture schematic: dual-graph input (structural morphometry + functional connectivity) into multi-scale adaptive graph attention blocks (Transformer-style) with fusion and output heads.
Brain maps across scales: layered cortical/region atlases showing morphological features and functional edges to illustrate multi-scale inputs.
Attention heatmaps overlaid on brain regions to show which structure–function links drive cognitive predictions (interpretability).
Performance / ablation charts: prediction accuracy vs. baselines and ablation of multi-scale/adaptive components.
paper_title: Learning Structural-Functional Brain Representations through Multi-Scale Adaptive Graph Attention for Cognitive Insight
paper_authors: Badhan Mazumder, Sir-Lord Wiafe, Aline Kotoski, Vince D. Calhoun, Dong Hye Ye
